source.title: Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering for Interpretable Attribute Control in Symbolic Music Generation
source.authors: Ioannis Prokopiou; Pantelis Vikatos; Maximos A. Kaliakatsos-Papakostas; Theodoros Giannakopoulos; Themos Stafylakis

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies inference-time steering of musical attributes, but does not test whether sparse features compete for limited representational capacity or are stored in superposition. Its vector-overlap and steering results concern a related but different question.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cosine similarity between Pitch and Duration steering vectors and compares dual-steering strategies. These results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not test the claim versions about superposition, capacity pressure, LLM features, SAE units, or the dimensionality of superposed features. Single-attribute and context-override results concern steering efficacy, not the claim.
record.test_reason: The study extracts DiffMean steering vectors for Pitch and Duration in a pre-trained symbolic music Transformer and compares dual-steering combination strategies. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only as support for the Linear Representation Hypothesis. It does not vary feature sparsity or count relative to dimensions. It does not study polysemantic neurons, train or evaluate SAEs, or test the dimensionality of superposed features. The 0.49/0.81 cosine overlap between two contrastive attribute vectors is a statement about correlated concept directions (the authors attribute it to corpus correlation). It is not evidence about superposition under capacity pressure. Steering success and quality degradation are steering-efficacy measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that MMT encodes pitch and duration as linear latent directions usable for training-free steering. They find All-to-All injection the most robust strategy, able to override extreme autoregressive contexts. They also conclude that Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization (Pitch priority) decouples the entangled attribute vectors better than simple addition. They draw no conclusions about superposition or capacity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DiffMean vectors and inference-time residual-stream steering, then compares vector-combination and orthogonalization strategies. It does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method or test its capacity claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Pitch and Duration vector cosine similarity varies by layer, peaking at Layer 3. Steering outcomes also vary by dual-steering strategy and by conditioned scenario.

fits_no_version.finding: In MMT, the DiffMean Pitch and Duration directions have an average absolute cosine of 0.49, peaking at 0.81 at Layer 3. Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization with Pitch priority gives higher dual-steering success (88.5% vs 85.2%) and lower degradation (2.14 vs 2.31) than simple addition. Symmetric SVD orthogonalization performs worst.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive attribute directions for correlated musical attributes overlap substantially in a symbolic music Transformer's residual stream. Asymmetric orthogonalization of these directions modestly improves joint steering.

record.problems: The study does not test feature capacity or superposition. The dual-steering comparison reports aggregate results for a 1,600-generation validation grid without uncertainty estimates in Table III. Quality degradation is described by the authors as a proxy for perceptual quality.
record.rows_left_out: Single-attribute unconditioned steering and single-attribute context-override results (Tables II and the Section IV-B text) were left out because they report steering efficacy, not superposition or the geometry/interference comparison captured here. Conditioned dual-steering scenario outcomes (Table IV) were also left out because they report steering performance without a comparison isolating feature overlap or superposition.

untested.parts: Not tested: sparse features outnumbering dimensions, nearly orthogonal overlapping storage, a sparsity-dependent phase transition, and regular geometry. No toy models are used.
Not tested: polysemantic neurons, and whether features compete for limited capacity with dedicated vs shared dimensions.
Not tested: polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
Not tested: neuron-level distribution of features and SAE recovery. The model is a music Transformer, not an LLM. SAEs are mentioned only as future work.
Not tested: SAE features as complete, stable, canonical units. No SAE is trained.
Not tested: whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. The paper steers along single DiffMean directions but does not compare against multi-dimensional feature structure.

record.verdict_notes: Toy Models of Superposition [5] is cited only for the linear representation idea. No uncertainty is reported for Table III, and only one model is studied. 'Entanglement' here means correlation between contrastive concept vectors, not feature interference from superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse feature count relative to network dimensions, capacity competition, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Does not study polysemantic neurons arising through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The model is a symbolic music Transformer, not an LLM; the paper does not measure feature distribution across neurons or SAE recovery.
Does not use or evaluate SAEs, or test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical.
Extracts and steers attribute vectors but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
